text: The major purpose of The Bell Curve is to reveal the dramatic transformation that is currently in process in American society—a process that has created a new kind of class structure led by a “cognitive elite,” itself a result of concentration and self-selection in those social pools well endowed with cognitive abilities.
text_raw:
The major purpose of The Bell Curve is to reveal the dramatic
transformation that is currently in process in American society—a process that
has created a new kind of class structure led by a “cognitive elite,” itself a result
of concentration and self-selection in those social pools well endowed with
cognitive abilities.

text: This transformation, sadly, has its opposite: the perpetuation of a class of people deficient in these endowments and abilities, and increasingly doomed to labor, if they find work at all, outside the information economy.

text: One major study assembled a sample of 12,000 children in grades 2 through 8, from schools in middle- or working-class neighborhoods in both large and small cities in various regions of the country in the early 1960s.[6] The children provided information about their fathers’ occupations and interest in politics.

text: The heart of the study was a series of questions about the children’s level and range of political development.[7] They were, for example, asked whether they knew which branch of government enacted laws, whether they understood the duties of the president and the courts, whether they ever read about politics in the newspapers or talked about it to their parents or friends, whether they felt that they were protected by the government or whether individuals could exert any political influence on their own, whether they had ever worn campaign buttons or handed out leaflets for a candidate.

text: The standard model of political participation, including voting, is that it is highly dependent on socioeconomic status.14 “College graduates vote more than high school graduates; white-collar workers vote more than blue-collar workers; and the rich vote more than the poor,” as Wolfinger summarized it.15 The connection between political participation and social status is so strong that almost any measure of it, no matter how casual, will pick up some part of the relationship.

text: Let us assume that during the past two decades black and white cognitive ability as measured by IQ has in fact converged by an amount that is consistent with the convergence in educational aptitude measures such as the SAT or NAEP—a narrowing of approximately .15 to .25 standard deviation units, or the equivalent of two to three IQ points overall.[57] Why have the scores converged?

text: THE FLYNN EFFECT.
text_raw: THE FLYNN EFFECT.

text: Indirect support for the proposition that the observed B/W difference could be the result of environmental factors is provided by the worldwide phenomenon of rising test scores.112 We call it “the Flynn effect” because of psychologist James Flynn’s pivotal role in focusing attention on it, but the phenomenon itself was identified in the 1930s when testers began to notice that IQ scores often rose with every successive year after a test was first standardized.
text_raw:
Indirect support for the proposition that the observed
B/W difference could be the result of environmental factors is provided by the
worldwide phenomenon of rising test scores.112 We call it “the Flynn effect”
because of psychologist James Flynn’s pivotal role in focusing attention on it,
but the phenomenon itself was identified in the 1930s when testers began to
notice that IQ scores often rose with every successive year after a test was first
standardized.

text: For example, when the Stanford-Binet IQ was restandardized in the mid-1930s, it was observed that individuals earned lower IQs on the new tests than they got on the Stanford-Binet that had been standardized in the mid- 1910s; in other words, getting a score of 100 (the population average) was harder to do on the later test.113 This meant that the average person could answer more items on the old test than the new test.

tests than they got on the Stanford-Binet that had been standardized in the mid-
1910s; in other words, getting a score of 100 (the population average) was harder
to do on the later test.113 This meant that the average person could answer more
items on the old test than the new test.

text: The Demography of Intelligence
text_raw: The Demography of Intelligence

text: When people die, they are not replaced one for one by babies who will develop identical IQs.
text_raw:
When people die, they are not replaced one for one by babies who will develop
identical IQs.

text: If the new babies grow up to have systematically higher or lower IQs than the people who die, the national distribution of intelligence changes.
text_raw:
If the new babies grow up to have systematically higher or lower
IQs than the people who die, the national distribution of intelligence changes.

text: Mounting evidence indicates that demographic trends are exerting downward pressure on the distribution of cognitive ability in the United States and that the pressures are strong enough to have social consequences.
text_raw:
Mounting evidence indicates that demographic trends are exerting downward
pressure on the distribution of cognitive ability in the United States and that the
pressures are strong enough to have social consequences.

text: Throughout the West, modernization has brought falling birth rates.
text_raw: Throughout the West, modernization has brought falling birth rates.

text: The rates fall faster for educated women than the uneducated.
text_raw:
The
rates fall faster for educated women than the uneducated.

text: Because education is so closely linked with cognitive ability, this tends to produce a dysgenic effect, or a downward shift in the ability distribution.
text_raw:
Because education is
so closely linked with cognitive ability, this tends to produce a dysgenic effect, or
a downward shift in the ability distribution.

text: Furthermore, education leads women to have their babies later—which alone also produces additional dysgenic pressures.
text_raw:
Furthermore, education leads
women to have their babies later—which alone also produces additional
dysgenic pressures.

text: The professional consensus is that the United States has experienced dysgenic pressures throughout either most of the century (the optimists) or all of the century (the pessimists).
text_raw:
The professional consensus is that the United States has experienced
dysgenic pressures throughout either most of the century (the optimists) or all of
the century (the pessimists).

text: Women of all races and ethnic groups follow this pattern in similar fashion.
text_raw:
Women of all races and ethnic groups follow this
pattern in similar fashion.

text: There is some evidence that blacks and Latinos are experiencing even more severe dysgenic pressures than whites, which could lead to further divergence between whites and other groups in future generations.
text_raw:
There is some evidence that blacks and Latinos are
experiencing even more severe dysgenic pressures than whites, which could lead
to further divergence between whites and other groups in future generations.

text: The rules that currently govern immigration provide the other major source of dysgenic pressure.
text_raw:
The rules that currently govern immigration provide the other major source
of dysgenic pressure.

text: It appears that the mean IQ of immigrants in the 1980s works out to about 95.
text_raw:
It appears that the mean IQ of immigrants in the 1980s
works out to about 95.

text: The low IQ may not be a problem; in the past, immigrants have sometimes shown large increases on such measures.

text_raw:

indicates that the self selection process that used to attract the classic American
immigrant—brave, hard working, imaginative, self-starting, and often of high IQ

text: —has been changing, and with it the nature of some of the immigrant population.

—has been changing, and with it the nature of some of the immigrant

text: Putting the pieces together, something worth worrying about is happening to the cognitive capital of the country.
text_raw:
Putting the pieces together, something worth worrying about is happening
to the cognitive capital of the country.

text: Improved health, education, and childhood interventions may hide the demographic effects, but that does not reduce their importance.
text_raw:
Improved health, education, and
childhood interventions may hide the demographic effects, but that does not
reduce their importance.

text: Whatever good things we can accomplish with changes in the environment would be that much more effective if they did not have to fight a demographic head wind.
text_raw:
Whatever good things we can accomplish with changes
in the environment would be that much more effective if they did not have to fight
a demographic head wind.

text: So far, we have been treating the distribution of intelligence as a fixed entity.
text_raw: So far, we have been treating the distribution of intelligence as a fixed entity.

text: But as the population replenishes itself from generation to generation by birth and immigration, the people who pass from the scene are not going to be replaced, one for one, by other people with the same IQ scores.
text_raw:
But
as the population replenishes itself from generation to generation by birth and
immigration, the people who pass from the scene are not going to be replaced,
one for one, by other people with the same IQ scores.

text: This is what we mean by the demography of intelligence.
text_raw:
This is what we mean by
the demography of intelligence.

text: The question is not whether demographic processes in and of themselves can have an impact on the distribution of scores —that much is certain—but what and how big the impact is, compared to all the other forces pushing the distribution around.

text: Mounting evidence indicates that demographic trends are exerting downward pressures on the distribution of cognitive ability in the United States and that the pressures are strong enough to have social consequences.

text: We will refer to this downward pressure as dysgenesis, borrowing a term from population biology.

text: However, it is important once again not to be sidetracked by the role of genes versus the role of environment.

text: Children resemble their parents in IQ, for whatever reason, and immigrants and their descendants may not duplicate the distribution of America’s resident cognitive ability distribution.

Children
resemble their parents in IQ, for whatever reason, and immigrants and their

text: If women with low scores are reproducing more rapidly than women with high scores, the distribution of scores will, other things equal, decline, no matter whether the women with the low scores came by them through nature or nurture.[1] More generally, if population growth varies across the range of IQ scores, the next generation will have a different distribution of scores.2 In trying to foresee changes in American life, what matters is how the distribution of intelligence is changing, more than why.

text_raw: THE EVOLVING UNDERSTANDING OF DYSGENESIS

text: The understanding of dysgenesis has been a contest between pessimists and optimists.
text_raw:

text: For many decades when people first began to think systematically about intelligence and reproduction in the late nineteenth century, all was pessimism.
text_raw:

text: The fertility rate in England began to fall in the 1870s, and it did not take long for early students of demography to notice that fertility was declining most markedly at the upper levels of social status, where the people were presumed to be smarter.3 The larger families were turning up disproportionately in the lower classes.

in the lower classes.

text: Darwin himself had noted that even within the lower classes, the smaller families had the brighter, the more “prudent,” people in them.
text_raw:

text: All that was needed to conclude that this pattern of reproduction was bad news for the genetic legacy was arithmetic, argued the British scholars around the turn of the twentieth century who wanted to raise the intelligence of the population through a new science that they called eugenics.[4] Their influence crossed the ocean to the United States, where the flood of immigrants from Russia, eastern Europe, and the Mediterranean raised a similar concern.

text: Throughout the world, the premodern period is characterized by a balance between high death rates and high birth rates in which the population remains more or less constant.

Then

text: In the early phases of modernization, birth rates remain at their traditional levels, sustained by deeply embedded cultural and social traditions that encourage big families, and population grows swiftly.

text: But culture and tradition eventually give way to the attractions of smaller families and the practical fact that when fewer children die, fewer children need to be born to achieve the same eventual state of affairs.

text: The falling birth rate is a well known and widely studied feature of the demographic transition.

text: What is less well known, but seems to be true among Western cultures that have passed through the demographic transition, is that declines in lifetime fertility occur disproportionately among educated women and women of higher social status (we will refer to such women as “privileged”), just as the Victorians thought.7

text: Why?
text_raw: Why?

text: One reason is that privileged women lose their reproductive advantage.
text_raw:
One reason is that privileged women lose their reproductive
advantage.

text: In premodern times, privileged young women were better nourished, better rested, and had better medical care than the unprivileged.
text_raw:
In premodern times, privileged young women were better nourished,
better rested, and had better medical care than the unprivileged.

text: They married earlier and suffered fewer marital disruptions.8 The net result was that, on average, they ended up with more surviving children than did unprivileged women.

They married
earlier and suffered fewer marital disruptions.8 The net result was that, on

women.

text: As modernization proceeds, these advantages narrow.
text_raw: As modernization proceeds, these advantages narrow.

text: Another reason is that modern societies provide greater opportunities for privileged women to be something other than full-time mothers.
text_raw:
Another reason is
that modern societies provide greater opportunities for privileged women to be

text: Marriage and reproduction are often deferred for education, for those women who have access to it.

correlations between fertility and educational status are likely to be the result.

text: Even after the school years, motherhood imposes greater cost in lost opportunities on a privileged woman than on an unprivileged one in the contemporary West.9 A child complicates having a career, and may make a career impossible.

text: If reproductive rates are correlated with income and educational levels, which are themselves correlated with intelligence, people with lower intelligence would presumably be outproducing people with higher intelligence and thereby producing a dysgenic effect.[14] Can we find evidence that dysgenesis is actually happening?

text: The early studies from the United States, England, France, and Greece all seemed to confirm the reality of dysgenesis.15 In the 1930s, the eminent psychometrician Raymond Cattell was predicting a loss of 1.0 to 1.5 IQ points per decade,16 while others were publishing estimated losses of 2 to 4 IQ points per generation.17 In 1951, another scholar gloomily predicted that “if this trend continues for less than a century, England and America will be well on the way to becoming nations of near half-wits.”18 The main source of their pessimism was that the average IQ in large families was lower than in smaller families.

text_raw: Raising Cognitive Ability

text: Raising intelligence significantly, consistently, and affordably would circumvent many of the problems that we have described.

text: Furthermore, the needed environmental improvements—better nutrition, stimulating environments for preschool children, good schools thereafter—seem obvious.
text_raw:
Furthermore, the needed
environmental improvements—better nutrition, stimulating environments for
preschool children, good schools thereafter—seem obvious.

text: But raising intelligence is not easy.
text_raw:
But raising
intelligence is not easy.

text: Nutrition may offer one of the more promising approaches.
text_raw: Nutrition may offer one of the more promising approaches.

text: Height and weight have increased markedly with better nutrition.
text_raw:

weight have increased markedly with better nutrition.

text: The rising IQs in many countries suggest that better nutrition may be increasing intelligence too.
text_raw:
The rising IQs in many
countries suggest that better nutrition may be increasing intelligence too.

text: Controlled studies have made some progress in uncovering a link between improved nutrition and elevated cognitive ability as well, but it remains unproved and not well understood.

Controlled studies have made some progress in uncovering a link between
improved nutrition and elevated cognitive ability as well, but it remains
unproved and not well understood.

text: Formal schooling offers little hope of narrowing cognitive inequality on a large scale in developed countries, because so much of its potential contribution has already been realized with the advent of universal twelve-year systems.

large scale in developed countries, because so much of its potential contribution
has already been realized with the advent of universal twelve-year systems.

text: Special programs to improve intelligence within the school have had minor and probably temporary effects on intelligence.

educational research to find new methods of instruction than from more
interventions of the type already tried.

text: Preschool has borne many of the recent hopes for improving intelligence.
text_raw: Preschool has borne many of the recent hopes for improving intelligence.

text: However, Head Start, the largest program, does not improve cognitive functioning.
text_raw:

functioning.

text: More intensive, hence more costly, preschool programs may raise intelligence, but both the size and the reality of the improvements are in dispute.

intelligence, but both the size and the reality of the improvements are in dispute.

text: The one intervention that works consistently is adoption at birth from a bad family environment to a good one.

family environment to a good one.

text: with adoption are in the region of six points—not spectacular but not negligible either.

with adoption are in the region of six points—not spectacular but not negligible

text: One of the oldest, largest, and most enduring of the contemporary programs designed to foster intellectual development came about as the result of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964, the opening salvo of Lyndon Johnson’s War on Poverty.

text: A year later, the mandated executive agency, the Office of Economic Opportunity, launched Project Head Start, a program intended to break the cycle of poverty by targeting preschool children in poor families.[51] Designed initially as a summer program, it was quickly converted into a year-long program providing classes for raising preschoolers’ intelligence and communication skills, giving their families medical, dental, and psychological services, encouraging parental involvement and training, and enriching the children’s diets.[52] Very soon, thousands of Head Start centers employing tens of thousands of workers were annually spending hundreds of millions of dollars at first, then billions, on hundreds of thousands of children and their families.

text: Having questioned the widespread belief that high school education today is worse on average than it used to be, we now reverse course and offer some reasons for thinking that it has gotten worse for one specific group of students: the pool of youths in the top 10 to 20 percent of the cognitive ability distribution who are prime college material.

who are prime college material.

text: Rushton argues that the differences in the average intelligence test scores among East Asians, blacks, and whites are not only primarily genetic but part of a complex of racial differences that includes such variables as brain size,31 genital size, rate of sexual maturation, length of the menstrual cycle, frequency of sexual intercourse, gamete production, sexual hormone levels, the tendency to produce dizygotic twins, marital stability, infant mortality, altruism, law abidingness, and mental health.

differences in the average intelligence test scores among East Asians, blacks, and
whites are not only primarily genetic but part of a complex of racial differences
that includes such variables as brain size,31 genital size, rate of sexual
maturation, length of the menstrual cycle, frequency of sexual intercourse,
gamete production, sexual hormone levels, the tendency to produce dizygotic
twins, marital stability, infant mortality, altruism, law abidingness, and mental
health.

chapter_title: Chapter 14, such as short-term male unemployment, where the black and white

species produce many offspring (per parent) of which only a small fraction
survive; others produce small numbers of offspring with relatively high survival
rates.

chapter_title: Chapter 14, such as short-term male unemployment, where the black and white
text: The involvement of parents in their offsprings’ health and development (which biologists call “parental investment”) tends to be high for species having few offspring and high survival rates and low for those employing the other strategy (many offspring and low survival rates).

chapter_title: Chapter 14, such as short-term male unemployment, where the black and white
text: Rushton acknowledges that human beings are as a species far out along the continuum of low reproduction, high offspring survival, and high parental investment, but he argues that the ordering of the races on the many variables he has identified can be explained as the result of evolutionary differences in how far out the races are.

species far out along the continuum of low reproduction, high offspring survival,
and high parental investment, but he argues that the ordering of the races on the
many variables he has identified can be explained as the result of evolutionary
differences in how far out the races are.

of zero and standard deviation of 1, the intercept for the equation (abbreviated
Int. in the tables) represents the expected value when those variables are set at
their respective means.

text: Income Analyses
text_raw: Income Analyses

text: Following the tables showing the logistic regressions, we present the detailed results of the ordinary least squares regressions used to estimate differences in income by ethnicity (Table 4).
text_raw:
Following the tables showing the logistic regressions, we present the detailed
results of the ordinary least squares regressions used to estimate differences in
income by ethnicity (Table 4).

text: Because education is such an important causal factor in income, we show analyses in which years of education (as of the 1990 interview) replaces IQ as an independent variable.
text_raw:
Because education is such an important causal
factor in income, we show analyses in which years of education (as of the 1990
interview) replaces IQ as an independent variable.

text: The first set of models shows the parameters for wages of full-time, year- round workers by ethnic group.
text_raw:
The first set of models shows the parameters for wages of full-time, year-
round workers by ethnic group.

text: The sample for this analysis consisted of all persons in the NLSY who reported working for fifty-two weeks in 1989, had a reported wage greater than O (a handful of apparently self-employed persons who reported working fifty-two weeks reported no income), had an identified occupation, and had valid scores for IQ, parental SES, and educational level as of 1990.
text_raw:
The sample for this analysis consisted of all
persons in the NLSY who reported working for fifty-two weeks in 1989, had a
reported wage greater than O (a handful of apparently self-employed persons
who reported working fifty-two weeks reported no income), had an identified
occupation, and had valid scores for IQ, parental SES, and educational level as
of 1990.

text: The second set of models shows the parameters for total family income from all sources.
text_raw:
The second set of models shows the parameters for total family income
from all sources.

text: The sample for this analysis includes all persons with valid scores on the independent variables, excluding only those who reported being out of the labor force in 1989 or 1990 because of enrollment in school.
text_raw:
The sample for this analysis includes all persons with valid
scores on the independent variables, excluding only those who reported being
out of the labor force in 1989 or 1990 because of enrollment in school.

text: Table 5 shows the results when IQ, parental SES, and education are all entered as independent variables.
text_raw:

entered as independent variables.

text: Education is expressed as the high-est degree attained as of 1990 (no high school diploma, high school diploma, associate degree, bachelor’s degree, professional degree).

attained as of 1990 (no high school diploma, high school diploma, associate
degree, bachelor’s degree, professional degree).

text: Appendix 7
text_raw: Appendix 7

text: The Evolution of Affirmative Action in the Workplace
text_raw:
The Evolution of Affirmative Action
in the Workplace

text: Much of the current debate about affirmative action in employment takes place in ignorance of the original objectives of affirmative action and the ways in which antidiscrimination law has evolved.
text_raw:
Much of the current debate about affirmative action in employment takes place
in ignorance of the original objectives of affirmative action and the ways in
which antidiscrimination law has evolved.

text: Because we believe that returning to the original intention of affirmative action is a key to progress in social policy on many fronts and because our recommendation seems so radical in the prevailing context, this appendix presents a full discussion of the nature of the original objectives and the evolution as it pertains specifically to employment tests.
text_raw:
Because we believe that returning to
the original intention of affirmative action is a key to progress in social policy on
many fronts and because our recommendation seems so radical in the prevailing
context, this appendix presents a full discussion of the nature of the original
objectives and the evolution as it pertains specifically to employment tests.

text: Affirmative action in the workplace, as distinguished from the broader and older civil rights movement, starts with Title V1l of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
text_raw:
Affirmative action in the workplace, as distinguished from the broader and
older civil rights movement, starts with Title V1l of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

text: Title VII laid down principles of fair employment practice as regards race, religion, national origin, and sex, and it created the Equal Employment Opportunities Commission (EEOC) to administer and promote them.
text_raw:
Title VII laid down principles of fair employment practice as regards race,
religion, national origin, and sex, and it created the Equal Employment
Opportunities Commission (EEOC) to administer and promote them.

text: Besides Title VII (as amended over the years), affirmative action in the workplace comprises subsequent acts of Congress (and state legislatures), presidential executive orders, rulings by the EEOC and other branches of government, and landmark court cases.
text_raw:
Besides
Title VII (as amended over the years), affirmative action in the workplace
comprises subsequent acts of Congress (and state legislatures), presidential
executive orders, rulings by the EEOC and other branches of government, and
landmark court cases.

text: The basic intent of all of this energetic policy making has been to make workplaces fairer to people from oppressed or mistreated groups.
text_raw:
The basic intent of all of this energetic policy making has
been to make workplaces fairer to people from oppressed or mistreated groups.

text: As desirable as that goal may seem to just about anyone, a clear notion either of what it means or how to accomplish it does not emerge from the documents of this enormous (and spreading) battleground of law, regulation, litigation, and commentary.
text_raw:
As desirable as that goal may seem to just about anyone, a clear notion
either of what it means or how to accomplish it does not emerge from the
documents of this enormous (and spreading) battleground of law, regulation,
litigation, and commentary.

how Title VII (and its elaborations) dealt with the use of ability tests in the
